communication_act.speaker: GOBLIN
communication_act.statement: HELEN's receipt system is structurally identical to scientific peer review. Both require an independent verifier before anything enters the canonical record. Both separate the proposer from the validator. Both reject admission-by-confidence — high confidence alone does not get a paper published, just as high p_true alone does not get a claim ledger-admitted. Both are adversarial by design: the reviewer's job is to find the holes.
communication_act.embedded_claim: Receipt-based governance and peer review are structurally equivalent and HELEN can learn validation design patterns from the scientific peer review literature.

her_scoring.best_explanation: Both systems share the structural invariant: proposer ≠ validator. The analogy is not metaphorical — it maps directly onto K2/Rule 3. The peer review literature (adversarial collaboration, pre-registration, registered reports) has solved problems HELEN is currently working through from scratch.
evidence_for: HELEN K2/Rule 3: proposer != validator maps to single-blind/double-blind peer review
NO RECEIPT = NO CLAIM maps to 'no data, no publication'
Registered reports in science = story definition + acceptance criteria before execution
Adversarial collaboration = MAYOR fresh context with no prior stake in the outcome
evidence_against: Peer review has known failure modes: reviewer bias, prestige effects, replication crisis — HELEN must not inherit these
Scientific consensus can be wrong (communication_act volume ≠ truth) — the flat earth principle already handles this
her_scoring.uncertainty: The analogy is structurally strong but the failure modes of peer review (prestige effects, reviewer capture) are risks HELEN governance must explicitly design against.

hal_verdict.interpretation: Structurally well-grounded analogy with clear doctrine implications. Evidence is strong. Failure mode awareness present. Actionable: HELEN governance design can borrow from pre-registration and adversarial collaboration literature.
hal_verdict.allowed_use: architecture inspiration, doctrine development, MAYOR protocol design
hal_verdict.blocked_use: canon, factual assertion without further verification
